Title: Shroud of Eden Created
Description: During the War of Unification, Consus, a scientist of the Isu, created the first Shroud of Eden to treat casualties of the war.

Title: Project Anthropos
Description:
Project Anthropos was an Isu project whose aim was the creation of the human race as a docile, subservient workforce.

Commissioned around 2161 Isu Era (c.75,145 BCE) under the supervision of the "Father of Understanding" Yaldabaoth, the "Mother of Wisdom" Saklas, and the "Sacred Voice" Samael,[1] Project Anthropos sought to create a species in the Isu's own image that was extremely resilient, but completely subservient.

Source: Staff of Hermes Trismegistus | Assassin's Creed Wiki
Title: Manufacture of Staff of Hermes Trismegistus
Description: During the Isu Era, the Isu Aletheia replicated her own consciousness into the Staff, such that in the future, she would be able to interact and help the staff wielder to master its power.

Title: Eve Triggers an Human-Isu War
Description: Eve steals an all-powerful ancient artefact known as an Apple of Eden from the Isu - a Piece of Eden with the potential to enslave humanity. Eve grabs Adam and the pair escape triggering a war between humans and Isu over the following decade.

Title: Adam and Eve Rebellion
Description:
Adam and Eve were two humans who possessed a rare immunity to the effects of the Pieces of Eden due to their hybrid Isu-human lineage. This made them pivotal figures in the human rebellion against the Isu. They stole an Apple of Eden from the Isu to lead a revolt against their creators, marking one of the first acts of human resistance. This event is crucial as it signifies the beginning of humanity's struggle for independence from the Isu. The rebellion of Adam and Eve showcases the inherent desire for freedom and autonomy in the face of oppression and control. Their actions would lay the foundational mythology for many human religions and cultures within the Assassin's Creed universe, symbolizing the eternal fight for freedom against tyranny.

Date is approx. The rebellion led by Adam and Eve is suggested to have occurred close to the time of the Toba catastrophe, as their actions are closely tied to the events leading up to the Isu civilization's downfall. Since the Toba event is a fixed point in real-world history (around 75,000 BCE), and the lore implies this rebellion was a significant factor leading up to the Great Catastrophe in the game universe, it makes sense to date it just before this cataclysmic event.

Title: Creation of the Pieces of Eden
Description:
The Pieces of Eden were created by the Isu as tools and weapons to control the human population, which had been engineered by the Isu to serve them. These artifacts harness a form of energy that can manipulate the neural pathways in the human brain, effectively bending people to the will of the user. The most well-known of these is the Apple of Eden, capable of creating illusions and controlling minds. Other examples include the Staff of Hermes Trismegistus, capable of healing and longevity, and the Sword of Eden, which can emit powerful energy blasts. The creation of these objects was a testament to the Isu's advanced technology and their desire to maintain dominion over humanity. Their usage, however, led to various rebellions and conflicts, both among the Isu themselves and between Isu and humans.

Date is approx. Since the Pieces of Eden were created by the Isu to control and manipulate humans, and given that the Isu civilization predates the Toba catastrophe of around 75,000 BCE, we can assume that these artifacts were created well before this event.

Title: The [Toba|Great|First] Catastrophe / Ragnarök
Description:
A cataclysmic event during human prehistory, caused by a coronal mass ejection, which saw the near total extinction of both humanity and the Isu who were in military conflict at the time. Consequently the Isu did not forsee the coming apocalypse until it was too late. Despite this, certain members of the First Civilization worked to find a means of suppressing it – or to at least protect future generations from the predicted recurrence – by researching ways of combatting the cataclysm within underground Vaults.

This event was a massive solar flare or a series of catastrophic events that nearly wiped out all life on Earth. It led to the downfall of the Isu and drastically reduced the human population. This event forced the remaining Isu to work alongside humans to rebuild and led to the eventual fading of the Isu into myth and legend.

Source: Leap of Faith | Assassin's Creed Wiki
Title: The First Leap of Faith
Description:
The Assassin tradition of the Leap of Faith evolved from an ancient practice that was performed by the Medjay of Egypt who were the only people who knew how to correctly perform the Leap and survive. A Medjay named Bayek of Siwa attempted to teach the Leap to his son, Khemu, but unfortunately Khemu was killed before he could learn it. 

The first mentions of Medjay date back to the Old Kingdom, where Medjay referred to citizens of the land of Medja. By the Eighteenth Dynasty during the New Kingdom, the Medjay were an elite paramilitary police force. [From "real-world" Wikipedia].

Title: Moses & The Staff of Eden
Description: Moses used the powers of a Staff of Eden to free the Israelites from Egyptian rule and to split the Red Sea during their escape.

Title: Order of the Ancients
Description: The Order of the Ancients was founded by Pharaoh Smenkhkare, with the goal of obtaining knowledge and artifacts previously possessed by the First Civilization. The group would later develop into the Order of the Knights Templar.

Title: Trojan War
Description: The Trojan War started due to an Apple of Eden, later believed to have been caused by the Isu Eris. The war saw the rise and fall of many famous heroes, including Achilles and Paris. Greek commander Agamemnon would later be revered by the Cult of Kosmos as a "servant of Kosmos".

Source: Staff of Hermes Trismegistus | Assassin's Creed Wiki
Title: Trismegistus Staff Bestowed to Pythagorus
Description: Around the 6th Century BCE, Hermes handed the staff over to the Greek philosopher Pythagoras in a remote desert. Pythagorus, living abnormally long using the staff, set out to learn more about the staff eventually discovering the secret ruins of Atlantis, with which the staff is connected.

Source: Spear of Leonidas | Assassin's Creed Wiki
Title: First Human to Wield the Spear of Leonidas
Description: The first known human to wield the spear was the first wife of King Anaxandridas II of Sparta and the mother of Leonidas I

Source: Staff of Hermes Trismegistus | Assassin's Creed Wiki
Title: Kassandra becomes Keeper of the Staff
Description: Around the 5th Century BCE, misthios Kassandra reached the entrance of Atlantis, encountering Pythagorus where he sealed Atlantis and relented the staff, immediately passing away in the absence of its powers. Kassandra later witnessed a recording from Aletheia asking her to hold onto the staff until she met the "Heir of Memories", fully embracing her role as Keeper of the Staff until then.

Source: Spear of Leonidas | Assassin's Creed Wiki
Title: Kassandra Passes Broken Spear Down to Herodotus
Description: Kassandra left the Spear to Herodotus as something to remember her by once its power was exhausted. The Spear was subsequently buried beneath the Book of Herodotus and laid untouched for centuries until 2018 when both objects were recovered by Layla Hassan

Source: Spear of Leonidas | Assassin's Creed Wiki
Title: Spear Passed Down Again to Leonidas' Daughter Myrinne
Description: After being broken during the Battle of Thermopylae, the broken tip was recovered by the Spartans and handed over to Leonidas' daughter Myrrine.

Game: Assassin's Creed: Legacy of the First Blade
Title: Natakas: Kassandra's Lover, Ancestor of Aya
Description: Natakas (killed in 422 BCE by a member of The Immortals) was the son of Darius, the assassin of King Xerxes I of Persia. He later gets together with Kassandra. Those two then produce a son, Elpidios, who is an ancestor of Origin's Aya or Amunet.

Source: Spear of Leonidas | Assassin's Creed Wiki
Title: Spear Passed Down Once More to Kassandra
Description: Myrrine would in return hand down the Spear to Kassandra on one occasion when she was seven years old.

Source: Spear of Leonidas | Assassin's Creed Wiki
Title: Spear Given to Leonidas I
Description: Leonidas was given the spear by his mother, wife of Anaxandridas II of Sparta, wielding it until his death in 480 BCE at the Battle of Thermopylae.

Source: Ezio Auditore da Firenze | Assassin's Creed Wiki
Title: Ezio & All Other Assassins Envisioned
Description: After the Cult of Kosmos had been defeated by the Spartan misthios Kassandra during the Peloponnesian War, she saw a vision of Ezio and all the Assassins that would follow her legacy in fighting against chaos. This premonition alluded to the war that would continue for centuries afterwards between the Assassins and the Templars.

Title: Bayek of Siwa is Born
Description: Bayek of Siwa (born c. 85 BCE), also known by the alias Amun, was one of the last Medjay of Egypt and the founder of the Hidden Ones alongside his wife, Aya.

Title: Khemu is Killed by the Order of Ancients
Description: The Order of the Ancients, a proto-Templar organization, murdered his son, Khemu, because the two refused to cooperate in unlocking the Siwa Vault for them.

Title: Reda in Egypt
Description: An Egyptian nomadic merchant and child prodigy. He made rounds throughout Lower Egypt and Cyrenaica with his camel Amun during the reign of Ptolemy XIII.

Title: Reda, 10 Years Later, Hasn't Aged a Day
Description: By 38 BCE, Reda also extended his travels to the Sinai and Upper Egypt, yet strangely had not seemed to have aged a day in the ten years since Bayek had last seen him.

Title: Reda, Centuries Later, in England
Description: Toured England accompanied by an Anglo-Saxon man during the reign of Alfred the Great as representative of the Thousand Eyes. He eventually met the Viking shieldmaiden Eivor Varinsdottir as she assisted the Raven Clan in settling their new home of Ravensthorpe.

Title: Birth of Altaïr Ibn-La'Ahad
Description: Altaïr was born to Assassin parents: a Christian mother, Maud, and a Muslim father, Umar Ibn-La'Ahad.Raised to be an Assassin from birth, Altaïr became a Master Assassin at age 24, an accomplishment unheard of for one so young.

Source: Leap of Faith | Assassin's Creed Wiki
Title: Show of Faith
Description: During the defense of Masyaf, Al Mualim ordered several Assassins to perform the Leap of Faith before the Knights Templar gathered before the fortress, both to proclaim that the Assassins did not fear death, and to successfully trigger an ambush that would rout the attackers.

Title: Altaïr Serves as Mentor to Assassin's Brotherhood
Description: Altaïr Ibn-La'Ahad (Arabic: الطائر ابن لا أحد‎, 1165 – 1257) was a member of the Levantine Brotherhood of Assassins who served as their Mentor from 1191 until his death in 1257. During his tenure as Mentor, through the knowledge of an Apple of Eden, Altaïr made several discoveries and inventions that greatly helped the Order's progression. His leadership saw to the spread of the Assassins' influence throughout the Old World.

Title: Altaïr kills Al Mualim
Description:
Upon retaking Masyaf, Altaïr witnessed Al Mualim's mind control over its people using the Piece of Eden. After a lengthy battle, Altaïr managed to defeat his Master and mortally wound him with his Hidden Blade. After Al Mualim uttered his last words, challenging Altaïr's strength of character and ability to destroy the Apple, the Piece of Eden rolled from his lifeless hand and activated.

Standing before a vast holographic image that projected from the orb, Altaïr was soon joined by Malik and his men, and together they observed the projection: a map of the world indicating the location of other Pieces of Eden.

Title: Altaïr Stops Ritual Removal of Assassin's Ring Finger
Description:
After earning the loyalty, respect and faith of almost the entire Order, Altaïr desired to tell the tale of his life, and began writing his Codex. As Mentor, he started to drastically change the methods and rituals practiced by the Order, encouraging low-profile techniques to effectively combat their Templar adversaries.

As the Assassins' main goal was to protect the people, Altaïr found the ritual removal of Assassins' ring fingers "a false promise of paradise" and the prohibition against poison to be useless. He redesigned the Hidden Blade so that it would not require the removal of the finger to function, and could dispense poison.

Title: Death of Altaïr Ibn-La'Ahad
Description:
In the decade that followed his reclamation of the Order, Altaïr began building a library underneath the Masyaf fortress, where he stored thousands of books containing knowledge he had gained from the Apple. 

Additionally, Altaïr began to disperse the Order, stating that it should be spread throughout the world rather than contained in Masyaf.

Altaïr returned to Masyaf's castle and, once he was sure it had been evacuated, met with his son outside the library, which he discovered was actually meant to be a vault, inside which Altair planned to seal the Apple of Eden and himself. 

Altaïr entered and locked the library before hiding the Apple behind a far wall. He then seated himself in a chair in the centre of the library, imprinting a memory onto his sixth and final seal. Once he had done so, Altaïr Ibn-La'Ahad laid his head to one side and, at the age of 92, finally and peacefully passed away.

Source: Ezio Auditore da Firenze | Assassin's Creed Wiki
Title: Ezio is Born
Description: Ezio was born in Firenze on 24 June 1459, as the second eldest child of Giovanni and Maria Auditore. Although he appeared to be stillborn at first, he began crying after some words of encouragement from his father. Giovanni remarked on the boy's "fine set of lungs" before proudly raising him in the air, naming him Ezio Auditore da Firenze.

Title: Ezio Initiated into the Brotherhood
Ezio Becomes Mentor of Italian Brotherhood
Death of Ezio
Description:
Ezio befriends the Ottoman Assassins, falls in love with Sofia Sartor and claims the final key to Altair's library/vault in Masyaf. Here, Ezio speaks to Desmond as he realises that the message held within the Apple is not for the Italian Assassin. An Isu called Jupiter appears who warns Desmond of a great calamity that's going to destroy the earth. Again. She shows Desmond the location of the Grand Temple where he can stop the second disaster occuring.

Ezio realises that he is a mere messenger and returns to Sophia who he marries and has two children with. It sounds like a happy ending but tragically, Ezio dies suddenly at 65 in a Florentine Piazza. His injuries from his 30 years spent as an Assassin are blamed and our hearts are crushed.

Title: Edward Kenway Is Born
Description: Edward James Kenway (1693 – 1735) was a Welsh-born British privateer-turned-pirate and a member of the West Indies and British Brotherhoods of Assassins.

Title: Edward Kenway Finds Hidden Blade
Description: The adventures of pirate Assassin Edward Kenway, experienced through DNA via the modern day Templar outfit Abstergo Entertainment, take place in the Caribbean in the 18th century. Edward actually doesn't start out as an Assassin, instead he finds a hidden blade after chasing down and murdering a member of the Brotherhood called Duncan Walpole.

Title: Baby Haytham Kenway is Born
Description: Upon receiving a pardon from Lord Walpole, he moved to London and joined the British Brotherhood, eventually gaining the rank of Master Assassin. While in London, he met Tessa Stephenson-Oakley, the daughter of the wealthy landowner from whom he rented his house. Using her family connections, Tessa assisted Edward in purchasing a manor on Queen Anne's Square, London, and by 1725, the two married and had a son, Haytham.

Title: Edward Kenway is Killed by Mercenaries
Description: On 3 December 1735, the Kenway household was infiltrated by masked men who kidnapped Jennifer and killed several of the servants. After making sure that his wife and son were safe, Edward raced to the games room and was confronted by two of the intruders. After a prolonged fight, one of the men managed to impale Edward through the chest with his sword, killing him instantly.

Title: Haytham Becomes First Grand Master of the Templar Order's Colonial Rite
Abstergo Formed
Description: Officially founded in 1937, Abstergo Industries was actually one small part of the Templar scheme to control the world through capitalism and scientific progress. Abstergo's origins lay in the perfection of the assembly line by Templar leaders Henry Ford and Ransom "Ranny" Olds, at the turn of the 20th century. The assembly line was an early means to control both workers and the capitalists who employed them, representing the first step in the Templars' goal to subjugate the world through economics.

Title: Abstergo Realisations
Description: Abstergo's research division was secretly working on a device capable of imitating the mind-controlling properties of a Piece of Eden across a network. In the same year, Abstergo developed its first fully-functional Animus device and began to seek out appropriate test subjects.

Source: Leap of Faith | Assassin's Creed Wiki
Description: In 2000, Daniel Cross performed a Leap of Faith into the Persian Gulf to escape the Assassins' Dubai headquarters, shortly after instinctively murdering the Mentor with his newly acquired Hidden Blade.

Title: The Second Disaster
Description:
The Second Disaster, so named because it was a recurrence of the Toba catastrophe that nearly destroyed the Isu civilization, was a would-be cataclysmic event on 21 December 2012 triggered by a coronal mass ejection great enough to devastate the entire Earth. Predicted, but ignored for much of recorded human history, it promised to see the near complete destruction of mankind.  

Ultimately, the calamity was prevented through the efforts of the Assassins, who, guided by messages left by the Capitoline Triad, journeyed to the Grand Temple that housed a device called the global aurora borealis device capable of generating a planetary shield. On the day of the disaster, the Assassin Desmond Miles used the device to protect Earth from the CME, at the cost of his own life, and the release of a vengeful Juno from the Grand Temple.

Source: Do the Isu still exist somewhere? | Ubisoft Forum
Title: One Isu Remains
Description:
An Isu named Juno surived the solar flare and was sealed in the Grand Temple. Desmond freed her in ACIII where she was able to upload herself into Abstergo computers in what she called "The Grey". Her plan was to become a real body with the Phoenix Project but was unable to due to her consciousness being spread too thin. 

Aletheia however technically lives in the Staff of Hermes is still alive. Until the staff is destroyed.

Source: Leap of Faith | Assassin's Creed Wiki
Title: Desmond's First Leap of Faith
Description: In 2012, Desmond Miles performed his first Leap of Faith in Monteriggioni, after witnessing a vision of Ezio climbing to a View Point due to the Bleeding Effect. A few months later, Desmond executed another, much higher Leap of Faith in New York City, jumping from the One World Trade Center, before deploying a parachute to glide to another rooftop.

Title: Olivier Garneau Killed by Watchdogs' Aiden Pearce
Description: Watch Dogs protagonist Aiden Pearce kills an employee of Abstergo, Olivier Garneau, who was marked as wanted by the Brotherhood when examined through ctOS. Thanks to a file found on Layla Hassan’s computer, Aiden Pearce’s involvement in Olivier’s death is confirmed canon crossover. In the file you can see an image of Aiden standing over Olivier firing a pistol into his back as panic ensues around him.

Source: Staff of Hermes Trismegistus | Assassin's Creed Wiki
Title: Staff Passed on to the Heir of Memories
Description: Layla Hassan and her Assassin cell find the entrance to Atlantis where she meets Kassandra (who was kept alive by the staff). Kassandra hands the staff over to Layla believing her to be the Heir of Memories, instructing her to destroy it. Inside, Layla continues to relive Kassandra's genetic memories from the throne room, accompanied by Victoria, where they were ambushed by Templars commanded by Juhani Otso Berg. Layla killed all but one, then murdered Victoria as she tried to intercept the bloodshed. Soon after Layla defeated Otso in combat leaving him paralysed and her immortal.

Source: Spear of Leonidas | Assassin's Creed Wiki
Title: Layla Hassan Recovers the Spear
Description: Using Kassandra's DNA found on the spear, Layla was able to relieve her memories through the Animus. Once Layla had found Atlantis and met Kassandra, kept alive by the Staff of Hermes Trismegistus, she tried offering the Spear back to her, only for Kassandra to reply that it was broken and that Layla could keep it.

Source: Gap in the Armous | Watch Dogs Wiki
Title: A Watch Dogs Leap of Faith
Description: A Deadsec recruit performs a Leap of Faith from a rogue ex-Albion prodigy 's flat building into Battlebridge Basin in Islington, London.

Source: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla: Every Main Character’s Age, Height, And Birthday
Title: Birth of Eivor Varinsdottir
Description: Eivor Varinsdottir, the canonical female protagonist of Assassin's Creed Valhalla, was born in the year 847 CE in Rygjafylke, Norway to parents Rosta and Varin. As a child, she survived a brutal wolf attack, earning her the nickname "Wolf-Kissed". Eivor carries the DNA and dormant memories of the Isu Odin.

Title: Eivor leads the Raven Clan to settle in England
Description: In 873 CE, Eivor Varinsdottir, leader of the Raven Clan, made the decision to leave Norway and sail to England to establish a new Viking settlement. Eivor's adoptive brother Sigurd had been away serving under King Styrbjorn and wanted to be his own ruler. Eivor and Sigurd took their clan and founded the settlement of Ravensthorpe in the Kingdom of Mercia, building it up on the site of an old camp used by the sons of Ragnar Lothbrok. From their new home, the Raven Clan sought to expand their influence by forging alliances with the kingdoms of England.

Title: Eivor is Laid to Rest in Vinland
Description:
Eivor's death year is not explicitly stated in the game. However, they are known to have been laid to rest in Vinland. Their legacy lives on through the stories of their adventures and leadership.

After her death, Eivor was ultimately buried in a grave by the Kanien'kehá:ka in Tsoka'we'kowáhne, the area which eventually became modern day Concord in Massachusetts, United States.

Assassin's Creed Valhalla doesn't explicitly state Eivor's age at the time of their death. However, we can make an educated guess based on historical context, narrative clues, and in-game lore. Eivor is depicted as a young adult capable of leading raids and battles when they lead their clan to England in 873. If we assume Eivor was in their late 20s to early 30s by that time, which is reasonable given their leadership role and combat prowess, we can make some further assumptions.

Given the typical life expectancy of the time, combined with Eivor's dangerous lifestyle, reaching an age significantly beyond 50 or 60 would be remarkable. However, Eivor is also shown to be exceptionally strong, resilient, and supported by advanced medicine (in the context of the setting) and perhaps even Isu genetics or technology, indirectly hinted at through their visions and connection to Odin.

The game's narrative suggests Eivor finds peace in their later years, with their grave located in Vinland (North America), indicating a life of exploration continued well beyond the main events of the game. Taking all of this into account, plus the narrative need for Eivor to have lived a full and adventurous life, a reasonable guess might place Eivor's age at death somewhere between 50 to 65 years old, possibly even reaching 70 if we account for the less historically accurate elements of the game that could extend a protagonist's life.

Without direct confirmation from the game or supplemental materials, this remains speculative, and Eivor's age at death is a topic open to interpretation based on the blend of historical setting and the series' fictional narrative.

Title: Birth of Basim Ibn Ishaq, human reincarnation of the Isu Loki
Description: In the year 835 CE, Basim Ibn Ishaq was born as a human reincarnation of the Isu Loki. Loki, along with other members of the Aesir, a faction of the Isu, had uploaded his consciousness to the Isu supercomputer Yggdrasil before the Great Catastrophe that destroyed the Isu civilization. This allowed Loki to leapfrog through time and be reborn centuries later in the human body of Basim during the 9th century Islamic Golden Age. Basim was born to parents Abdel Moujahid and Zohra in the Abbasid Caliphate, unaware of his Isu origins and memories as Loki.

Title: Basim Ibn Ishaq joins the Hidden Ones and becomes an Assassin
Description: Basim Ibn Ishaq began his journey from street thief to master assassin in Baghdad during the Islamic Golden Age. Taken under the wing of Hidden Ones leader Roshan, Basim trained in the ways of the order, learning to master assassination techniques, parkour, and the Creed. Through Basim's initiation, Assassin's Creed Mirage serves as an origin story drawing parallels to Altaïr Ibn-La'Ahad's own journey to master assassin 300 years later. Basim's path to becoming a full-fledged Hidden One was a key turning point that would come to define his life, setting the stage for his future actions and the fate that awaited him.

Title: Basim Ibn Ishaq awakens as the reincarnation of the Isu Loki
Description:
After joining the Hidden Ones and rising to the rank of Master Assassin, Basim Ibn Ishaq began to awaken to his true identity as the Sage, a human reincarnation of the Isu Loki. Loki's memories, long suppressed within Basim, started to surface, driving Basim to uncover the truth of his existence.

Basim traveled to Norway and attempted to reveal to Sigurd Styrbjornsson, the Sage of Tyr, his own Isu identity in the hopes of finding an ally. When Sigurd rejected this truth, Basim manipulated him into searching for the Saga Stone, an Isu vault key. Basim's ultimate goal was to access the Yggdrasil supercomputer and fully restore Loki's consciousness within himself. 

As Loki's memories continued to merge with Basim's own, his personality began to change, his goals and loyalties shifting away from the Hidden Ones and towards his Isu past and unfinished business. This awakening would put Basim on a collision course with Eivor Varinsdottir, the reincarnation of Odin, culminating in a fateful confrontation years later inside the Yggdrasil chamber.

Title: Basim Ibn Ishaq betrays Eivor and reveals his true identity as Loki
Description:
After years of manipulating Sigurd and searching for the Yggdrasil chamber, Basim Ibn Ishaq's true intentions were finally revealed to Eivor Varinsdottir. Inside the ancient Isu temple in Norway, Basim turned on Eivor, announcing that she, not Sigurd, was his intended target all along.

Basim exposed Eivor as the reincarnation of Odin, while unveiling himself to be the Sage of Loki, on a mission of vengeance against the Aesir. The two engaged in a climactic battle, with Basim attempting to kill Eivor to open the Yggdrasil supercomputer and fully restore his Isu identity. After an intense fight spanning multiple phases, Eivor ultimately defeated Basim. With Sigurd's help, she trapped Basim inside the Yggdrasil machine, imprisoning his consciousness in the Grey, a digital realm between life and death. This final confrontation brought an end to Basim's schemes, but also set the stage for his eventual release and reawakening in the modern day, nearly 1150 years later.

Title: Basim Ibn Ishaq is released from the Yggdrasil supercomputer into the modern world
Description:
In 2020, over 1100 years after his imprisonment by Eivor in the Yggdrasil supercomputer, Basim Ibn Ishaq was finally released back into the physical world. Assassin Layla Hassan, while exploring Yggdrasil through her Animus, encountered Basim's consciousness trapped within the Grey, the digital realm between life and death.

Basim, having fully awakened as the Sage of Loki, convinced Layla to free him. In exchange, he provided her with the knowledge needed to prevent the impending catastrophe that would destroy the Earth. Layla agreed and uploaded Basim's consciousness into a spare reincarnation of Eivor's body she had found. 

Reborn in a new, younger form, Basim emerged into the 21st century, his goals as Loki still unfulfilled. He immediately set out to find the Isu Aletheia and continue his search for his long-lost children. Basim's release marked a new chapter in the millennia-spanning saga of the Isu and their connection to humanity, setting the stage for future conflicts and revelations in the ongoing struggle between the Assassins and Templars.

Title: Birth of Hytham in the Abbasid Caliphate
Description:
Hytham was born sometime in the 850s CE in the Abbasid Caliphate, which at the time was experiencing a golden age of scientific and cultural advancement under the rule of the Abbasid dynasty. The exact year and location of Hytham's birth are unknown, but it likely occurred in the region of Iraq or Persia.

The Abbasid Caliphate, which lasted from 750 to 1258 CE, saw the translation of many ancient Greek and Roman texts, leading to significant developments in mathematics, astronomy, medicine, and other fields. It was into this intellectually vibrant world that Hytham was born, setting the stage for his future as a scholar and member of the Hidden Ones.

Title: Young Hytham encounters Basim in Baghdad
Description:
Basim Ibn Ishaq has a chance encounter with a young boy while synchronizing a viewpoint in the Karkh district of Baghdad. This child, named "Young Eagle" (Hytham in Arabic), is already perched atop the tower, frightened to climb back down.

In conversation, the boy reveals that the Hidden Ones avenged his mother's death, sparking his desire to join their ranks. Basim, recognizing Hytham's potential, encourages him to seek out the Brotherhood when he comes of age, foreshadowing Hytham's future as an Assassin.

Title: Hytham becomes Basim Ibn Ishaq's apprentice in the Hidden Ones
Description:
Sometime in the 870s CE, nearly a decade after their first encounter in Baghdad, Hytham officially became an apprentice to Basim Ibn Ishaq in the Hidden Ones, the precursor organization to the Assassin Brotherhood.

Their partnership would eventually lead them far beyond the borders of the Abbasid Caliphate, as they sailed to England in 873 CE alongside Sigurd Styrbjornsson to aid the Raven Clan in establishing a new settlement.

Title: Asgardian Isu upload their DNA and consciousness to Yggdrasil
Description:
In approximately 75,000 BCE, with the impending threat of the Great Catastrophe that would devastate the Earth, Odin and 8 of his Asgardian Isu followers devised a plan to survive. Using a special mead and the Yggdrasil supercomputer, they encoded their DNA into human genomes, allowing them to be reborn as human reincarnations in the distant future.

Odin, along with Tyr, Thor, Freyja, Heimdall and others, imprinted their genetic data into the Yggdrasil device. This would allow their Isu consciousnesses to awaken within their human descendants millennia later, albeit with their memories muddled by the lens of Norse mythology. 

The Asgardian Isu saw this as a way to cheat death and reclaim their power after the world had recovered from the cataclysm. Unbeknownst to Odin, Loki, a rival Isu, secretly added his own genetic imprint to the human bloodline as well, setting the stage for his reincarnation's future conflict with Odin's.

Title: Loki secretly uploads his own DNA and consciousness to Yggdrasil
Description:
In approximately 75,000 BCE, as Odin and his Asgardian followers prepared to upload their DNA into the human gene pool using the Yggdrasil supercomputer, Loki made his own plans. Unbeknownst to the others, Loki snuck into the Yggdrasil chamber and surreptitiously added his genetic code to the machine, ensuring he too would be reborn in the future.

Loki's calculations differed from Odin's, and he was not deemed worthy to be included in the Asgardians' plans for reincarnation. Determined to survive the Great Catastrophe in his own way, Loki killed one of the Aesir and took their place in the upload ceremony. This allowed Loki's DNA and consciousness to be preserved in Yggdrasil alongside the others. 

Loki's deception would lay the groundwork for his eventual reincarnation as Basim Ibn Ishaq in 9th century Baghdad, setting the stage for his future conflict with Odin's own sage, Eivor Varinsdottir. Loki's covert use of Yggdrasil was a crucial step in his long game of revenge against the Aesir who had wronged him in the Isu era.

Title: Eivor and Sigurd discover the Yggdrasil supercomputer in Norway
Description:
Eivor Varinsdottir and her adoptive brother Sigurd Styrbjornsson journeyed deep into the wilderness of Hordafylke, Norway, following Sigurd's visions of a great tree and a mysterious chamber. Their quest led them to Goinnhellir cave, where they found an ancient Isu vault hidden behind a wall of ice.

Using his knowledge of the Isu language gleaned from his visions as the reincarnation of Tyr, Sigurd opened the vault and the pair descended to the heart of the complex. There they discovered the Yggdrasil, a colossal tree-like supercomputer created by the Isu to preserve their consciousness and memories. 

In front of the Yggdrasil stood a large spherical device, similar to the one Desmond Miles activated to protect the Earth from a coronal mass ejection in 2012. Sigurd, compelled by his Isu identity, interfaced with the device, transporting his and Eivor's minds into a simulation of Valhalla contained within Yggdrasil. 

Inside the simulation, Eivor encountered Odin's memories imprinted on her DNA, while Sigurd communed with his own Isu past as Tyr. The discovery of the Yggdrasil marked a pivotal moment in the siblings' journey to understand their roles as Sages and the ancient conflict between the Isu that they had inherited.

Title: Basim attempts to kill Eivor in the Yggdrasil chamber but is defeated and imprisoned
Description:
Basim Ibn Ishaq, fully awakened as the reincarnation of the Isu Loki, confronted Eivor Varinsdottir in the Yggdrasil chamber hidden beneath Norway. Realizing that Eivor, not Sigurd, was the reincarnation of his nemesis Odin, Basim attacked, seeking to kill Eivor as revenge for Odin's treatment of Fenrir in the Isu era.

After an intense battle, Eivor defeated Basim. With Sigurd's help, she trapped Basim's consciousness inside the Yggdrasil supercomputer, imprisoning him in a state between life and death. This act mirrored Odin's own imprisonment of Loki in Isu times, repeating the cycle of their ancient conflict. Basim would remain trapped within Yggdrasil for over 1100 years until his eventual release in 2020.

Title: Eivor recovers the Crystal Ball Piece of Eden from Gorm Kjotvesson in Vinland
Description:
During her journey to the North American region of Vinland, Eivor Varinsdottir of the Raven Clan confronted Gorm Kjotvesson, a member of the Order of the Ancients. Gorm had been sent to Vinland with a Crystal Ball, one of the Pieces of Eden, in an attempt to access an Isu vault known as the Grand Temple. Eivor assassinated Gorm, taking possession of the Crystal Ball, unaware of its true origins or power.

Eivor chose to entrust the Crystal Ball to the Kanien'kehá:ka tribe, the same Native American tribe that Ratonhnhaké:ton (Connor) from Assassin's Creed III would be born into centuries later. The Kanien'kehá:ka would continue to protect the Crystal Ball and the Grand Temple for generations, until Connor collected the artifact and the key to the temple during the events of Assassin's Creed III, burying them for Desmond Miles to unearth in the future.

Title: The Staff of Hermes Trismegistus passes from Layla Hassan to Basim Ibn Ishaq
Description:
Layla Hassan used the Staff of Hermes Trismegistus, an ancient Isu artifact that granted its wielder biological immortality, to enter the Yggdrasil supercomputer in an attempt to prevent a catastrophic solar flare. Inside the simulation, Layla encountered the consciousness of Basim Ibn Ishaq, who had been trapped there for centuries following his failed attempt to kill Eivor Varinsdottir in 9th century Norway.

Basim, the reincarnation of the Isu Loki, manipulated Layla into sacrificing her life to prevent the disaster. As Layla's physical body perished, she dropped the Staff, which landed on Basim's remains inside Yggdrasil. This allowed Basim to absorb the Staff's power, healing his body and freeing him from his digital prison. Now restored and wielding the Staff of Hermes Trismegistus, Basim emerged into the modern world, ready to resume his centuries-old quest for vengeance against the Isu Odin and his own lost children.

Title: Birth of Jacob and Evie Frye, twin Assassins of the Victorian era
Description:
On November 9, 1847, fraternal twins Jacob and Evie Frye were born in Crawley, England to Ethan Frye, a schoolmaster, and his wife Cecily, both members of the British Assassin Brotherhood. Tragically, their mother Cecily died while giving birth to the twins.

As the children of Assassins, Jacob and Evie were raised from an early age to follow in their parents' footsteps. Under the tutelage of their father Ethan, they began their lifelong training to become skilled Assassins themselves, setting the stage for their pivotal roles in the secret war against the Templars that would define their adult lives.

Title: Jacob and Evie Frye are inducted into the British Brotherhood of Assassins
Description:
During the 1860s, twins Jacob and Evie Frye officially joined the British Brotherhood of Assassins after being trained from a young age by their father, Ethan Frye. As children of Assassin parents, Jacob and Evie were raised from birth to one day take up the mantle themselves.

Under Ethan's tutelage, the twins honed their skills in stealth, combat, and parkour, as well as studying the history and tenets of the Assassin Order. By 1868, both Jacob and Evie were fully fledged Assassins, working alongside their father to protect London from Templar influence. However, that same year, Ethan passed away from pleurisy, leaving his children to carry on the fight without him. The Frye twins' induction into the Brotherhood marked the beginning of their lifelong commitment to the Assassin cause and the events that would lead them to liberate London from Templar control.

Title: Death of Jacob and Evie Frye
Description:
The exact dates of Jacob and Evie Frye's deaths are unknown. What is certain is that they were still alive in 1916, when Jacob's granddaughter Lydia Frye was an active Assassin.

At some point after this, likely in the early to mid 20th century, both Jacob and Evie passed away, presumably from old age. As they were born in 1847, they would have been at least in their late 60s in 1916. Their deaths marked the end of an era for the British Brotherhood, which they had led and strengthened for decades following their liberation of London from Templar control in 1868.

Title: Kassandra seals the lost city of Atlantis
Description:
After defeating the four mythical creatures - the Minotaur, the Cyclops, Medusa, and the Sphinx - and collecting their artifacts, Kassandra returned to the ancient Isu city of Atlantis. There, she met with her true father, Pythagoras, who had been using the Staff of Hermes Trismegistus to keep himself alive for centuries.

Pythagoras, hesitant to seal away the knowledge of Atlantis forever, resisted Kassandra's attempts. The misthios was then faced with a choice: convince Pythagoras to willingly hand over the Staff and seal Atlantis peacefully, or fight him for control of the powerful Piece of Eden. Regardless of the choice made, Kassandra obtained the Staff and used it in conjunction with the four artifacts to seal the gates of Atlantis, preventing the city's advanced technology and knowledge from falling into the wrong hands. This marked the end of the mythical city's story, and the beginning of Kassandra's long tenure as the Keeper of the Staff.

Title: Kassandra defeats the Cult of Kosmos, foreshadowing the Templar Order
Description:
The Spartan misthios Kassandra successfully eliminated key members of the Cult of Kosmos, a secret society that sought to control all of Greece from the shadows. The Cult, led by Aspasia, aimed to bring order and stability to the Greek world through manipulation and control, believing that free will was the root of all chaos.

Kassandra's actions led to the downfall of the Cult, but the ideological seeds that drove them would persist. The Cult of Kosmos served as a precursor to the Order of the Ancients in Ptolemaic Egypt and eventually the Templar Order, which would continue to pursue similar goals of control and order throughout history. The methods and beliefs of the Cult foreshadowed the eternal struggle between the Assassins, who fight for free will, and the Templars, who seek to impose their vision of order. Kassandra's victory over the Cult marked a temporary setback for these ideals, but the conflict would re-emerge time and again in different forms.

Title: Darius becomes the first proto-Assassin to use the hidden blade
Description:
Darius, a Persian assassin, became the first recorded wielder of the iconic hidden blade weapon that would later become synonymous with the Assassin Brotherhood. Darius used this concealed blade to assassinate King Xerxes I of the Achaemenid Empire.

Darius' assassination of Xerxes was in response to the king's growing tyranny and oppression. This act established Darius as a proto-Assassin, fighting against the abuse of power and promoting free will, ideals that would later be codified in the Assassin's Creed. His use of the hidden blade set a precedent for the signature weapon of the Assassins, which would be passed down through the generations. Darius' legacy as the first to use the hidden blade in the fight against tyranny marks a significant milestone in the Assassin Brotherhood's long history.

Title: Birth of Kassandra in Sparta
Description:
In the year 458 BCE, Kassandra was born on the Greek island of Sparta to King Leonidas I and his wife Gorgo. As a newborn, Kassandra was condemned to death by the Spartan Cult due to a prophecy foretelling her terrible future. However, Kassandra's mother defied the Cult's decree and spared her life by passing her off to Myrinne, Leonidas' first wife.

Myrinne raised Kassandra as her own on the island of Kephallonia, far from Sparta. This act set Kassandra on her path to become a legendary Spartan mercenary and misthios who would play a pivotal role in the Peloponnesian War and the eternal conflict between the Isu and their human descendants. Kassandra's birth, though nearly prevented by the Cult, allowed her to grow into a powerful warrior whose actions would ripple across centuries.

Title: Bayek and Aya found the Hidden Ones, precursor to the Assassin Brotherhood
Description:
In 47 BCE, after eliminating the leaders of the Order of the Ancients in Egypt, Bayek of Siwa and his wife Aya laid the foundations for the Hidden Ones, the earliest form of the Assassin Brotherhood.

Guided by the principles of the Will of the Creed, Bayek and Aya established a bureau for the Hidden Ones on the island of Philae near the Nile. Here they began recruiting and training new members, creating a network of allies across the Mediterranean dedicated to protecting the free will of all people. 

The Hidden Ones took an oath to never compromise the human will, upholding the ideals that Bayek and Aya had fought for against the oppressive Order. With the Hidden Ones, the two laid the groundwork for the centuries-long conflict between the Assassins and Templars over humanity's right to make its own decisions free from the control of any single individual or group.

Title: Aya's journey to Rome and formation of the Hidden Ones bureau
Description:
After defeating the Order of the Ancients in Egypt alongside her husband Bayek, Aya made the decision to travel to Rome in 47 BCE to continue her fight against the remnants of the Order there. Adopting the alias "Amunet", she infiltrated Roman society and began recruiting new initiates to the Hidden Ones' cause.

Over the next few years in Rome, Aya/Amunet systematically tracked down and eliminated the last of the Order's leadership, including figures like Brutus, Cassius, and Septimius. Her efforts culminated on March 15, 44 BCE with the assassination of Roman dictator Julius Caesar himself, dealing a major blow to the Order's influence. 

With Caesar gone, Aya focused on establishing the Hidden Ones' first organized bureau in Rome, training more recruits in the ways of the Assassins. This cemented the Hidden Ones' presence in the heart of the Roman Empire and laid the groundwork for the future growth of the Brotherhood across Europe in later centuries.

Title: Creation of the Ankh by the Isu
Description:
The Ankh was an ancient and powerful Piece of Eden created by the Isu during their reign on Earth thousands of years ago. It took the form of an Egyptian cross with a looped top, a symbol that would later become synonymous with eternal life in Ancient Egyptian culture.

The Ankh possessed incredible powers of regeneration and healing. When grasped, it could rapidly restore injuries and even revive the dead by restarting their bodily functions. This made the Ankh one of the most powerful artifacts forged by the advanced Isu civilization. 

While the exact details of its creation remain unknown, the Ankh's regenerative abilities were likely intended to aid the Isu's efforts to survive the coming Great Catastrophe that ultimately devastated their species. The Ankh's existence was just one example of the incredible technological marvels produced by the precursor Isu race. 

In the modern day, the Ankh resurfaced in Egypt, where it played a pivotal role in the events of Assassin's Creed Origins. Its powers allowed the Hidden One Bayek to revive his wife Aya after she was killed by members of the Order of Ancients, setting her on the path to help establish the earliest foundations of the Assassin Brotherhood.

Title: Death of Altaïr Ibn-La'Ahad, Mentor of the Levantine Assassins
Description:
In the decade following his reclamation of the Assassin Order, Altaïr Ibn-La'Ahad began constructing a vast library beneath the Masyaf fortress to store the immense knowledge he had gained from the Apple of Eden. This library would ultimately become his final resting place.

As Altaïr grew older, he came to the realization that the Assassins should not be concentrated solely in Masyaf. He began dispersing members of the Order across the world to expand their reach and influence. 

Finally, at the age of 92 in 1257 CE, Altaïr returned to Masyaf's castle one last time. Ensuring it had been fully evacuated, he met with his son Darim outside the library entrance. Altaïr revealed the library was not simply a repository of knowledge, but an ancient vault meant to seal himself and the Apple of Eden away forever. 

Altaïr entered the vault alone, hiding the Apple behind a far wall before taking a seat in the library's center. There, the legendary Mentor imprinted his final memory seal before peacefully passing away, his long life and decades of leadership over at last. His sacrifice safeguarded the Apple's power for centuries until his descendant Desmond could eventually rediscover it in the modern era.

Title: Birth of Arno Victor Dorian in Versailles
Description:
On August 26, 1768, Arno Victor Dorian was born in Versailles, the Kingdom of France, to Charles Dorian, a French Assassin, and his Austrian wife Marie. Arno was born into a noble family that had long been loyal members of the Assassin Brotherhood.

Tragically, Arno's father Charles was murdered when Arno was still a child, leaving him an orphan. He was subsequently adopted as a ward by the wealthy de la Serre family, who unbeknownst to Arno were actually members of the Templar Order, sworn enemies of the Assassins.

Title: Arno Victor Dorian joins the French Brotherhood of Assassins
Description:
In the year 1789, at the onset of the French Revolution, Arno Victor Dorian made the decision to join the French Brotherhood of Assassins in Paris. This choice was driven by his desire to seek redemption for the death of his father Charles Dorian, who had been an Assassin himself before being murdered when Arno was a child.

After being framed for the murder of François de la Serre, the Grand Master of the Templar Order who had adopted Arno, he was imprisoned in the Bastille. There he met fellow inmate Pierre Bellec, an Assassin who had known Arno's father. Bellec encouraged the disillusioned Arno to follow in his father's footsteps and join the Brotherhood's fight against the oppressive Templar control over French society. 

When the Bastille was stormed on July 14th, 1789, Arno escaped and sought out the Assassin Council, officially inducting himself into their ranks. Despite his privileged upbringing by the Templars, Arno's natural charisma, combat skills, and determination to uncover the truth behind his father's murder made him a promising recruit for the Assassins as they aimed to guide the revolutionary spirit of France.

Title: The Sword of Eden and Arno's confrontation with Germain at the Temple
Description:
In 1794, Arno Dorian, a newly inducted member of the French Brotherhood of Assassins, tracked the Sage François-Thomas Germain to the ancient Temple of the Ancients located beneath the King's Garden in Paris.

Germain, a high-ranking Templar, was seeking to claim the Sword of Eden - a powerful Piece of Eden capable of channeling energy to disintegrate targets. This legendary Isu weapon had been hidden away in the Temple vault by Jacques de Molay, the last Grand Master of the Templar Order, in 1307. 

When Arno caught up to Germain, the two engaged in a climactic battle over the possession of the Sword. Despite Germain's mastery of swordsmanship, Arno managed to wrest the Sword from his grasp. However, in the chaos, Arno's lover Élise de la Serre, who had infiltrated the Templars, was accidentally struck down by the Sword's energy blast. 

Though he defeated Germain, the loss of Élise was a devastating blow to Arno. The Sword of Eden, with its ability to project deadly force fields, had once again demonstrated the immense power and danger posed by the ancient Isu artifacts to anyone who wielded them.

Title: Demond Miles is Born
Description: Desmond Miles (13 Mar 1987 - ) was a traveling hermit, and is a descendant to a long line of ancestors who had sworn their allegiance to the Assassin Order.  Raised on "The Farm" with numerous other families of the order by his parents, he was specifically trained to defend himself and become an Assassin.  As a teenager, he ran away from home, honing his learned skills to do so--even as his mother insisted he didn't.  He eventually found his way to New York City where he became a bartender.  He steadily assimilated into city life, even attending clubs on a regular basis.  Whenever asked, he told people he was raised by "hippies" or "conspiracy theorists," as he truly believed this was factual.

Title: Desmond Miles is abducted by Abstergo Industries
Description:
In September 2012, Desmond Miles, a bartender living in New York City, was kidnapped by agents of Abstergo Industries, the public face of the modern-day Templar Order. Under the orders of Daniel Cross, a Templar sleeper agent, Desmond was taken to an Abstergo facility located in Italy.

There, Desmond was forced into the Animus, a revolutionary machine created by Abstergo's Animus Project that allowed him to relive the genetic memories of his ancestors. Specifically, Desmond was made to experience the life of Altaïr Ibn-La'Ahad, a Master Assassin from the 12th century during the Third Crusade. 

Abstergo's goal was to use the Animus to locate powerful artifacts known as Pieces of Eden, created by an ancient precursor race called the Isu. As a descendant of Altaïr and other Assassins, Desmond's genetic memories held the key to finding these First Civilization relics before the Assassin Brotherhood could.

Desmond's abduction marked the beginning of his reluctant induction into the millennia-old conflict between the Assassins, who fight for peace and free will, and the Templars, who desire peace through control. His experiences in the Animus would awaken his own latent Assassin abilities and set him on a path to escape Abstergo's clutches.

Title: Desmond discovers the Pieces of Eden through Altaïr's memories
Description:
In 1191, while experiencing the genetic memories of his ancestor Altaïr Ibn-La'Ahad through the Animus, Desmond Miles first learned about the existence of powerful artifacts known as the Pieces of Eden.

After defeating his former mentor Al Mualim, who had been using an Apple of Eden to mind control others, Altaïr took possession of the ancient relic. As Altaïr held the glowing sphere, a vast projection appeared, displaying a map that indicated the locations of other Pieces of Eden across the globe. 

Through the bleeding effect, Desmond witnessed these events from Altaïr's perspective, realizing for the first time that the Assassins and Templars had been waging a secret war over these First Civilization artifacts for centuries. The Apple, and other Pieces of Eden like it, were incredibly advanced technological relics left behind by an ancient race that predated modern humanity. 

This revelation marked a turning point for Desmond. No longer was he simply being forced to relive his ancestor's memories - now he had insight into the true scope of the conflict between Assassins and Templars over these powerful remnants of the past. His journey to understand the Pieces of Eden, and keep them from the wrong hands, had begun.

Title: Desmond Miles experiences the Bleeding Effect
Description:
In September 2012, Desmond Miles was forced into an Animus by Abstergo Industries and made to relive the genetic memories of his ancestors like Altaïr Ibn-La'Ahad and Ezio Auditore da Firenze. However, due to his prolonged time experiencing these memories, Desmond began exhibiting the "Bleeding Effect."

The Bleeding Effect caused Desmond to subconsciously adopt the skills, personality traits, and abilities of his Assassin ancestors. He gained incredible free-running abilities, combat prowess, Eagle Vision, and even began taking on personality quirks of Altaïr and Ezio. Essentially, the more time Desmond spent in the Animus, the more his mind "bled" with his ancestors'. 

What started as simple headaches and bleeding noses escalated to Desmond instinctively performing Leaps of Faith and engaging in parkour across cities like Rome and Constantinople. By the time he escaped Abstergo in December 2012, Desmond had fully embraced the Assassin skills and knowledge imparted by the Bleeding Effect. 

This phenomenon allowed Desmond to awaken his own latent Assassin abilities inherited from his ancestors. While initially reluctant, the Bleeding Effect transformed Desmond into a capable modern-day Assassin, blurring his own identity with those of Altaïr, Ezio and others as he took up their centuries-long fight against the Templars.

Title: Desmond escapes Abstergo and joins the Assassin Rebellion
Description:
In December 2012, after being forced by Abstergo to relive the memories of his ancestor Altaïr Ibn-La'Ahad, Desmond Miles finally managed to escape the Templar facility in Italy with the help of Lucy Stillman, an undercover Assassin.

Fleeing to the United States, Desmond was brought to the Assassin Rebellion's base, hidden beneath the Grand Temple in New York City. There he was reunited with his father William Miles and met other Assassins like Shaun Hastings and Rebecca Crane. 

The Rebellion had been searching for Desmond for years, recognizing his importance as a descendant of several prominent Assassins whose genetic memories could help locate powerful Pieces of Eden. Under William's guidance, Desmond began embracing his Assassin heritage and training to master the skills he had subconsciously gained through the Bleeding Effect. 

His escape marked a pivotal turning point where Desmond transitioned from an unwilling captive of the Templars to an ally of the Assassins in their age-old conflict. Surrounded by his fellow Assassins, Desmond took his first steps towards the role he would eventually play in preventing a catastrophic solar event and confronting the Isu entity Juno.
